apiKey.summary: ApiKeyInput (1010 lines) is live in exactly two configurations — providerType 'pi_api_key' (the "I use other provider" card and Edit of pi/pi_compat connections) and 'anthropic' (Edit of anthropic connections; the standalone anthropic_api_key card is a dead step) — and in both the corp filter reduces 22 presets to {Anthropic, OpenAI, Custom}. Its unique live capabilities are: the two official-API preset arms whose submit shapes deliberately carry NO customEndpoint (pi+piAuthProvider or native anthropic — the merged form must not flatten these into the customEndpoint shape or the server force-converts them to pi_compat); the Custom preset's protocol toggle that both sets customEndpoint.api and derives piAuthProvider; the keyless-loopback local-endpoint path; empty-key-keeps-credential edit semantics; and the whole C3 catalog block (fetch/pick/probe/sync-toggle with tristate modelsSyncedAt), whose picker is already extraction-ready but whose enrolled-state prefill is missing on the real edit path (AiSettingsPage never passes syncModelsFromEndpoint). Dead weight is large: three providerType arms, the entire branded-preset economy (nessy-gateway JWT autofill, manifest, minimax/kimi/openrouter prefills), a literally-impossible 'ollama' arm, and the Bedrock + 3-tier arms — the latter two dead in the default desktop build but still edit-reachable through connections nessy-cli creates in the shared config, so the merge must re-route those edits rather than silently sending them to a form without the arms.

byo.stateMachine:
ENTRY (creation): ProviderSelectStep card 'custom_runtime' (ProviderSelectStep.tsx:142-158) — the card has no flag of its own, shown iff flags.nessy_codex || flags.nessy_claude. useOnboarding.handleSelectProvider (useOnboarding.ts:657-668) sets step='byo-runtime' with byoRuntimeProviderType=undefined (no lock), byoRuntimeIsEditing=false. ENTRY (edit): AiSettingsPage.handleEditConnection → resolveConnectionEditTarget → jumpToByoRuntime (useOnboarding.ts:929-944) with LOCKED providerType and prefill from byoRuntimeInitialValues(connection, storedKey).

RUNTIME RADIO: ByoRuntimeStep.tsx:77-98. availableRuntimes derives from window.electronAPI.getProviderFlags() (nessy_codex/nessy_claude — same build-time flags gating the provider cards, read over IPC). Optimistic default {codex:true, claude:true} because a flag-fetch failure means the IPC is unavailable (playground/stale preload), not that the runtimes are off; if both flags resolve false the form still offers both ('a dead form cannot be submitted' fallback, line 97). lockedProviderType collapses the list to one and hides the radio (rendered only when availableRuntimes.length > 1, line 164). A settle effect (104-109) snaps providerType onto availableRuntimes[0] once flags land. Initial selection: lockedProviderType ?? 'codex-runtime'.

VALIDATION (pure, apisetup/byo-runtime.ts:validateByoRuntimeForm:104-129, order matters): (1) baseUrl trimmed non-empty → 'endpointRequired'; (2) isNessyGatewayBaseUrl(baseUrl) → 'endpointIsGateway' — whole-URL match against the corp gateway chat base (trailing-slash-normalized; nessy-gateway.ts:79-80, backend twin upstream-target.ts:34-37). Rejected rather than warned for two concrete reasons documented at byo-runtime.ts:86-102: a {kind:'nestor'} upstream authenticates with the dp JWT and never reads the typed key (attachUpstreamCredential returns early for non-openai-compatible targets), and canEditLlmConnection/isNessyGatewayConnection would classify the saved row as the corp connection and hide its Edit button forever. Same host on a different path stays allowed (AGENTS.md custom-endpoint rule). (3) parseModelList(models) must yield ≥1 id → 'modelRequired'; (4) apiKey may be blank only when isEditing (blank = keep stored credential) OR isLoopbackBaseUrl(baseUrl) (localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 incl. bracketed IPv6 — renderer's single copy at byo-runtime.ts:74-83, mirroring server-core connection-setup-logic.ts:isLoopbackBaseUrl/setupTestRequiresApiKey) → else 'apiKeyRequired'.

SUBMIT PIPELINE (useOnboarding.handleSubmitByoRuntime:777-838): status idle → validating → BLOCKING live test via TEST_LLM_CONNECTION_SETUP carrying { provider:'anthropic' (legacy discriminator), runtimeProviderType: data.providerType, apiKey (blank when masked/empty), baseUrl, model: models[0] }. runtimeProviderType is what selects the driver: resolveSetupTestConnectionHint (factory.ts:441-476) returns { providerType: runtimeProviderType } FIRST, before any customEndpoint/pi branch — without it the test would classify as pi_compat and run through Pi. The runtime drivers answer the test structurally, not with a real turn (testCodexRuntimeConnection / testClaudeRuntimeConnection — spending a gateway/user-endpoint turn to answer 'is this configured' was declined). Edit-path escape hatch: keyIsUnverifiable = no usable key AND editingSlug — a blank/masked key means 'keep stored', which the test cannot see; its only possible verdict is 'API key is required', so that failure must not block the save (788, 799). Any other test failure blocks. Then buildByoRuntimeSetup → SETUP_LLM_CONNECTION → on success: onConfigSaved, credentialStatus 'success', step 'complete'. Server-side, the RPC's setupTestRequiresApiKey(baseUrl) independently allows keyless tests only for loopback (llm-connections.ts:335, 365-367).

WHY buildByoRuntimeSetup NEVER emits customEndpoint (byo-runtime.ts:145-168, useOnboarding.ts:763-776): the SETUP handler at server-core/handlers/rpc/llm-connections.ts:111-127 rewrites providerType to 'pi_compat' whenever a customEndpoint accompanies a configured baseUrl (`updates.customEndpoint = customEndpoint; updates.providerType = 'pi_compat'`), plus the anthropic-template branch at 78-89 does the same upgrade for anthropic providerTypes. A runtime connection converted to pi_compat routes through Pi and its local codex-responses-adapter never starts. This exact conversion shipped as a live bug: AiSettingsPage used to route every non-Pi connection to the anthropic_api_key form, whose submit attaches customEndpoint — editing a BYO runtime connection silently stopped it being one. Hence also the deliberately non-function providerType literals in BUILT_IN_CONNECTION_TEMPLATES for 'codex-custom'/'claude-custom' (connection-setup-logic.ts:237-246): the anthropic-api row's (hasCustomEndpoint)=>'pi_compat' form would do the same conversion at creation.

byo.summary: ByoRuntimeStep is a deliberately thin four-field form (runtime radio, endpoint, key, models) whose every decision lives as pure functions in apisetup/byo-runtime.ts, and whose entire architecture is organized around one landmine: the SETUP handler rewrites any customEndpoint-bearing payload to providerType 'pi_compat' (llm-connections.ts:111-127), which kills the local codex-responses-adapter — so buildByoRuntimeSetup never emits that field, the connection test names its runtime outright via runtimeProviderType (hint short-circuit in factory.ts), the codex-custom/claude-custom templates pin literal providerTypes, and the Edit path locks the runtime behind resolveConnectionEditTarget. The merged form's Pi arm inverts every one of those choices on purpose (it must emit customEndpoint to BE rewritten to pi_compat), so the arm switch becomes the guard around a known production bug class. Everything else the directive needs already has a seam: the C3 picker is standalone by design and its fetch/probe RPCs key only off baseUrl+key (work for all three arms unchanged, gated to the OpenAI protocol); the protocol toggle ports from ApiKeyInput's Custom preset but is Pi-arm-only until the adapter's UpstreamTarget union grows the anticipated anthropic-messages member — verified: BYO runtime upstreams are chat-completions-only today; metadata sync requires widening the pi_compat-only enrollment predicate and having the form stamp modelsSyncedAt; miniModel is new LlmConnection storage (catalog order is the current lever, plus the updateLlmConnection-allowlist drop trap). LocalModelStep (flag-off by default) is a 150-line prefill shell over exactly what the merged Pi arm produces: it submits baseUrl + models + customEndpoint {api:'openai-completions'} with no key, and resolveCustomEndpointSetup already maps keyless-loopback to authType 'none' / name 'Local Model' — the merged form's keyless-loopback path (which the runtime arms also support via isLoopbackBaseUrl + authType 'none') subsumes it entirely; only the Ollama defaults (localhost:11434, qwen3-coder) would need to survive as a preset or placeholder.

design.mergedForm:
MERGED FORM SPEC — single BYO/personal-key form (extends ByoRuntimeStep; ApiKeyInput retires from creation)

== 1. Card (ProviderSelectStep) ==
One card replaces two: keep id 'custom_runtime', re-copy as "Use your own key or endpoint" / desc "Connect an API key or a custom endpoint — run it on the Pi agent, Claude Code, or Codex." The 'api_key' card ("I use other provider") is REMOVED (ProviderSelectStep.tsx:136-140 + CHOICE_TO_METHOD row useOnboarding.ts:633).
Visibility: flags.api_key || flags.nessy_codex || flags.nessy_claude (today: nessy_codex||nessy_claude only, ProviderSelectStep.tsx:155-157). NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_API_KEY acquires a new meaning: it gates the Pi ARM of the merged form (and with it the official presets), no longer a separate card.

== 2. Field layout (top to bottom) ==
(1) Runtime segmented control — [Pi agent | Claude Code | Codex]
  - Values: arm type MergedEndpointArm = 'pi' | 'claude-runtime' | 'codex-runtime' ('pi' is an ARM id, not a providerType — the server derives pi/pi_compat/anthropic from the payload shape).
  - Availability: 'pi' iff flags.api_key; 'claude-runtime' iff flags.nessy_claude; 'codex-runtime' iff flags.nessy_codex. Same getProviderFlags IPC + optimistic all-on default + settle effect as today (ByoRuntimeStep.tsx:77-109); if flags impossibly resolve to none, offer all (dead-form guard, :97). Hidden when only one arm available or when locked (edit). Default selection: 'pi' when available, else first available.
  - Per-arm helper line under the control: Pi — "Runs on the built-in Pi agent. Supports OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible APIs."; Claude Code / Codex — "Runs the <harness> coding harness through a local adapter. OpenAI-compatible endpoints only."
(2) Endpoint section
  - Pi arm ONLY: preset dropdown {Anthropic, OpenAI, Custom} — port exactly VISIBLE_ENDPOINT_PRESET_KEYS (ApiKeyInput.tsx:181) and those three Preset rows (:117-118,:137: urls api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com/v1 / '', placeholders sk-ant-…/sk-…/'Paste your key here…'). Default preset: 'anthropic' (preserves the removed card's first-run "paste an Anthropic key and go" path). NONE of the other 19 hidden presets port. Anthropic/OpenAI preset: baseUrl input HIDDEN (submit baseUrl=undefined). Custom preset: baseUrl input shown; typing a URL re-resolves the preset via getPresetForUrl over the 3-preset list (api.anthropic.com snaps back to Anthropic; resolvePresetStateForBaseUrlChange ports as-is).
  - Runtime arms: plain required Endpoint input as today (autoFocus, helper "Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible chat/completions API, including /v1").
  - Gateway rejection (whole-URL, trailing-slash-normalized, isNessyGatewayBaseUrl) applies to ALL THREE arms — extension to the Pi arm is new but forced: NESSY_GATEWAY_PROVIDER_TYPES includes pi_compat (nessy-gateway.ts:35-39), so a Pi-arm save on that URL becomes permanently un-editable and its key would collide with Nestor-Token semantics. Same-host-different-path stays allowed (AGENTS.md).
(3) Protocol control — [OpenAI Compatible | Anthropic Compatible]
  - VISIBLE ONLY on the Pi arm with the Custom preset (port of ApiKeyInput.tsx:644-676, incl. helper "Most third-party APIs (Ollama, vLLM, DashScope) use OpenAI Compatible."). Default 'openai-completions'.
  - HIDDEN AND PINNED to openai-completions on the Claude Code and Codex arms. Proof this is not a UX choice: UpstreamTarget (packages/codex-responses-adapter/src/nestor-client.ts:32-36) has exactly {kind:'nestor'} and {kind:'openai-compatible'}; resolveUpstreamRequest (:61-81) posts `${baseUrl}/chat/completions` + Bearer; buildCodexRuntimeUpstream (drivers/codex.ts:32-38) and buildClaudeRuntimeUpstream (drivers/anthropic.ts:23-32) can only produce those two kinds. An Anthropic-compatible upstream for the runtime arms means adding the anticipated third union member plus body translation — an adapter feature, out of this plan's scope.
  - HIDDEN on Anthropic/OpenAI official presets (no customEndpoint is ever attached there).
(4) API key — password input, always shown on every arm (no Bedrock arm in this form). Requiredness: blank allowed iff isEditing (keep stored credential) OR loopback baseUrl (localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 incl. bracketed IPv6 — the single renderer copy isLoopbackBaseUrl, byo-runtime.ts:74-83, mirroring server setupTestRequiresApiKey). Masked '••' handling UNIFIED across arms: masked counts as key-present, is never sent in any payload, and makes the blocking test's key verdict non-blocking on edit (keyIsUnverifiable). This deliberately fixes the latent ApiKeyInput edit defect where the masked GET_API_KEY prefill is submitted verbatim to the pre-save test (handleSubmitCredential has no '••' detection — verified absent, useOnboarding.ts:407-516).
(5) Models — comma-separated input; contract line kept verbatim: "first model is the default, the last is used for summarization" (Pi contract; on runtime arms the last-entry rule also feeds getMiniModel's fallback). Shown on: runtime arms always; Pi arm Custom preset always; HIDDEN on Pi official presets (the server installs Pi default catalogs: llm-connections.ts:162-166). Required on runtime arms and on Pi Custom preset (see validation matrix). NO COMPAT_ANTHROPIC_DEFAULTS prefill on Custom — the current prefill of four claude-* ids (ApiKeyInput.tsx:420-421) is wrong for every non-Anthropic endpoint; the merged form starts empty with placeholder "e.g. deepseek-v3, deepseek-r1".
(6) C3 catalog block — [Fetch models button + published count] + ModelCatalogPicker + [Check access probes] — shown when baseUrl non-empty AND effectiveProtocol==='openai-completions'. effectiveProtocol: runtime arms = pinned 'openai-completions' (so the picker IS available on all runtime arms — the RPC branch needs only baseUrl+apiKey, llm-connections.ts:339-363 / openai-compat.ts, and the probe's 1-token chat/completions POST is exactly the wire the runtime adapter speaks); Pi Custom = the toggle value. ModelCatalogPicker is reused UNCHANGED (props-in/selection-out; selection writes ids.join(', ') back into the Models field). Manual fallback: the Models field always accepts free text; fetch failure shows catalogError and leaves manual entry usable. Anthropic-protocol Pi arm: no catalog block at all; helper under Models: "Anthropic-style APIs don't publish a model catalog with context data — enter model ids manually." (matches the isModelSyncEnrolled rationale, model-fetchers/index.ts:44-47).
(7) Utility model (miniModel) — NEW optional field, shown whenever the Models field is shown. A small select over the parsed Models list (plus free-text escape), placeholder "Defaults to the last model in the list." Stored as NEW LlmConnection.miniModel?: string. getMiniModel returns it first when set AND it passes the managed allowlist (explicit choice beats the keyword heuristic, never beats managed policy); all existing connections (no field) keep today's exact heuristic incl. the last-entry fallback the gateway claude card's ordering relies on. Validated at SETUP time: when models non-empty, miniModel must be one of them (else reject like validateModelList does for defaultModel).
(8) Auto-sync toggle — "Keep model metadata in sync with this endpoint" — same gate as the catalog block (openai-completions + baseUrl). Tristate contract preserved exactly: submitted ONLY when touched; absent=leave persisted, true -> modelsSyncedAt=Date.now(), false -> null (useOnboarding.ts:290-292; server llm-connections.ts:107-109). Edit prefill = connection.modelsSyncedAt != null — FIXING the AiSettingsPage gap (:882-889 never passes it) for every edit route of the merged form.
(9) Error banner (parseTestConnectionError-normalized test failures + save failures); Back; Continue with "Connecting…" loading text.

== 3. Submit shapes (the two-shapes rule is the architecture) ==
ARM 'claude-runtime' / 'codex-runtime' — buildByoRuntimeSetup unchanged in spirit, extended fields: { slug: claude-custom/codex-custom(-N) or editingSlug; credential? (non-blank, non-masked only); authType: 'api_key_with_endpoint'|'none' via credential||hasStoredKey; baseUrl; defaultModel: models[0]; models; miniModel?; modelsSyncedAt?: number|null (tristate, touched-only) }. NEVER customEndpoint, NEVER piAuthProvider, NEVER modelSelectionMode. Blocking test: TEST_LLM_CONNECTION_SETUP { provider:'anthropic' (legacy), runtimeProviderType, apiKey (blank when masked), baseUrl, model: models[0] } — structural driver test, keyIsUnverifiable escape on edit.
ARM 'pi' — routed through the existing pi_api_key pipeline (apiSetupMethodToConnectionSetup method 'pi_api_key' + handleSaveConfig), NOT a new payload builder:
  - Anthropic preset: { apiKey, baseUrl: undefined, connectionDefaultModel: undefined, models: undefined, piAuthProvider:'anthropic', modelSelectionMode:'automaticallySyncedFromProvider' } -> slug pi-api-key(-N) -> server: providerType 'pi' + rename "Nessy Backend (Anthropic)" + Pi default models (llm-connections.ts:154-166). NO customEndpoint — flattening this into the customEndpoint shape would pin it pi_compat and lose default-model sync.
  - OpenAI preset: same with piAuthProvider:'openai'.
  - Custom preset: { apiKey?, baseUrl (REQUIRED — see validation), customEndpoint:{ api: protocol }, piAuthProvider: protocol-derived 'anthropic'|'openai' (resolveCustomEndpointPayload semantics), connectionDefaultModel: parsed[0], models, modelSelectionMode: parsed.length>0 ? 'userDefined3Tier' : 'automaticallySyncedFromProvider', miniModel?, syncModelsFromEndpoint? (touched-only) } -> server deliberately rewrites to pi_compat (llm-connections.ts:111-128); keyless loopback -> authType 'none' + name 'Local Model' (resolveCustomEndpointSetup) — this SUBSUMES LocalModelStep.
  - lastNonCustomPreset silent fallback DIES: the Custom preset now requires a baseUrl, so the only path that consumed it (custom preset + empty baseUrl -> silent official-anthropic submit) is closed; protocol-derived piAuthProvider covers every remaining custom submit.
  - Pre-save test: provider 'pi' + piAuthProvider + customEndpoint (custom preset) or provider 'pi' + piAuthProvider (official presets); loopback keyless exemption preserved (setupTestRequiresApiKey server-side, :335/:365-367).

== 4. Edit mode ==
resolveConnectionEditTarget (byo-runtime.ts:205-217) becomes the single router with FOUR targets:
  - 'codex-runtime'/'claude-runtime' -> merged form, arm locked (unchanged).
  - 'pi_compat' (has customEndpoint) -> merged form, Pi arm locked, preset 'custom', customApi prefilled from connection.customEndpoint.api, sync toggle prefilled from modelsSyncedAt!=null, miniModel prefilled.
  - 'pi' with piAuthProvider in {anthropic, openai, undefined} AND no bedrock/3-tier shape -> merged form, Pi arm locked, preset = piAuthProvider ?? 'anthropic'; 'anthropic' (plain providerType) -> merged form, Pi arm, preset 'anthropic', but submit maps through the anthropic_api_key setup shape (drops piAuthProvider/modelSelectionMode — preserving today's byte-level reset semantics at llm-connections.ts:83-88 instead of silently renaming the connection to "Nessy Backend (…)").
  - EVERYTHING ELSE ('pi' with exotic piAuthProvider: amazon-bedrock, openrouter, google, minimax…, i.e. CLI-created connections) -> legacy ApiKeyInput edit surface, kept alive edit-only with its Bedrock and 3-tier arms intact. The api_key CARD dies; the ApiKeyInput FORM stays mountable via jumpToCredentials until an owner decision retires the exotic arms.
Arm is ALWAYS locked on edit (changing providerType is a different operation; the SETUP handler has no path for it — the historical conversion bug's rationale, useOnboarding.ts:923-928). Editable: baseUrl (still gateway-rejected), key (blank/masked keeps stored; adding a key to a keyless connection flips authType back to keyed; demotion to 'none' remains unreachable), models list/order, protocol (Pi Custom only — changes customEndpoint.api + piAuthProvider within pi_compat, allowed), miniModel, sync toggle. Not editable: arm, slug, display name (rename stays the separate AiSettingsPage dialog). Prefill via extended byoRuntimeInitialValues + the masked GET_API_KEY contract.

== 5. Validation matrix (order matters, first failure wins) ==
| Check | Pi/Anthropic preset | Pi/OpenAI preset | Pi/Custom | Claude Code | Codex |
| endpoint required | n/a (hidden) | n/a | YES (new tightening) | YES | YES |
| endpoint != gateway URL (whole match) | n/a | n/a | YES (new) | YES | YES |
| >=1 model id | n/a (hidden; SDK catalog) | n/a | YES | YES | YES |
| miniModel in models list | n/a | n/a | when set | when set | when set |
| key required | YES unless isEditing | YES unless isEditing | unless isEditing OR loopback | unless isEditing OR loopback | unless isEditing OR loopback |
| masked '••' key | key-present, not sent, keyIsUnverifiable on edit | same | same | same | same |
Blocking pre-save test on every arm; only the key-verdict is skippable (keyIsUnverifiable), any other failure blocks.

== 6. Model-metadata sync extension (BYO runtime enrollment) ==
(a) Form: runtime arms gain the same sync toggle; buildByoRuntimeSetup stamps modelsSyncedAt: number|null on touch (SETUP persists it generically already, llm-connections.ts:107-109).
(b) Predicate: isModelSyncEnrolled (model-fetchers/index.ts:48-52) widens to: [pi_compat && customEndpoint.api==='openai-completions' OR isAdapterRuntimeProvider(providerType) && !isNessyGatewayBaseUrl(baseUrl)] && typeof modelsSyncedAt==='number'. Gateway one-click connections can never enroll (no stamp is ever written for them, and the URL guard is belt-and-braces).
(c) Routing: _doRefresh takes the merge-never-replace branch (fetchOpenAiCompatModels + mergeModelMetadata + 24h TTL + restamp) for enrolled adapter-runtime connections BEFORE falling through to GatewayRuntimeModelFetcher; unenrolled non-gateway runtime connections keep today's behavior (empty fetch, layer-2 keep). Runtime upstreams are OpenAI-shaped by construction so the fetcher applies as-is.
(d) Timers: startAll/refreshNow suppress the hourly GatewayRuntimeModelFetcher timer for ENROLLED runtime connections (extend the `isNestor || isEnrolledByo` continue, index.ts:277) — the 24h TTL is their cadence, same as enrolled pi_compat.

EDIT-FALLBACK KEEPS ApiKeyInput COMPILED: the exotic-connection edit surface preserves the Bedrock and 3-tier arms as reachable code; deleting them 'because the card died' would strand CLI-created connections (apps/cli writes arbitrary piAuthProvider incl. amazon-bedrock into the shared config) — deletion needs its own owner decision, not a drive-by.
